text:
anya: Hey — running into a weird typing/structured-output issue with the Python async client when using tool/function calling. Repro below, tiny snippet:
```py
from redwood import AsyncClient
client = AsyncClient(api_key="REDACTED")

async def main():
    res = await client.tool.call("parse_order", {"text": "qty: 3"}, output_schema={"type": "object", "properties": {"qty": {"type": "integer"}}})
    # expecting {'qty': 3} (int) according to schema/TypedDict, but getting {'qty': '3'} (str)
    print(res)
```
matt: can you confirm which SDK version and model/tool config? is this hitting the new structured-output parser or the legacy json-fixup?
anya: 0.9.7 pre-release, using the new tool.call api. Model is gpt-like local test harness. output_schema above. The SDK returns the field as a string ("3") even though schema says integer. No intermediate transform on my side.
sara: ugh. thanks for the repro. quick hypothesis: async codepath currently shells out to the streaming parser which doesn't run the schema coercion step we added in sync Tool.run. So numbers become strings if model returns them with quotes.
anya: that matches what I see. any recommended workaround?
matt: short-term: coerce manually with jsonschema.validate + type conversion, or call the sync variant from a threadpool (ugly). also `from redwood.utils import coerce_output_types` may help if you can import it.
anya: tried coerce_output_types, it works but it's ugly for callers — defeats the "structured output" promise.
sara: created issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/2345 — flagged as regression. devx-bot: Issue #2345 created by sara: "async tool.call skips schema coercion -> incorrect types in structured output".
devx-bot: linked PR template: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pulls
matt: for the longer-term fix we'll: (1) make schema coercion part of the async postprocess pipeline, (2) improve type hints so callers using TypedDict get correct return types in stubs (ToolResult[MyTypedDict] -> await returns MyTypedDict), and (3) add a small sample in samples/python/toolcall-typed-output demonstrating end-to-end.
anya: Would it be possible to get a temporary doc note in the SDK README about this behavior? Saved me some hours.
sara: yes — I'll add a short "async caveat" section in the next patch release, and open the PR to fix the async coercion in the same cycle. I'll also add a unit test and an e2e sample. Planning P1 for the fix.
anya: awesome, thanks. leaving the repro in the issue with logs.
matt: assign to sara, tagging infra for test infra if needed. :thumbsup:
sara: assigned, thanks. I'll update here when PR is opened.
anya: thanks all!
